newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU experts meet to discuss large grain crop.
newsitem.headline: EU experts meet to discuss large grain crop.

text.p: European Union experts are meeting on Thursday morning to discuss what is expected to be another bumper grain harvest this year, farm officials said.

No figures were circulated in advance of the meeting of national grain delegates, being held in Brussels, but the European Commission said last week it expected a crop of 200 million tonnes against a record 201.5 million last year.

European officials have started to express concern over the large crop, especially of feed grain, saying it could blow a hole in the EU's cautious export subsidy budget and raise the chances of tension over subsidies with Washington.
A new July/June grain export campaign gets under way later on Thursday when the EU holds its first weekly tender for refunds to export wheat, barley and rye to world markets.
Competition is expected to be fairly tough this season but the continued sharp rise in the dollar and flood problems in eastern Europe may help Brussels cut costs and boost demand.
A stronger dollar, sitting above six French francs for the first time in four years, reduces spending on export refunds.
Thursday's exchange of views on harvests is part of a routine expert-level meeting of grain officials ahead of a formal cereals management committee session later on Thursday.
Also on the expert-level agenda are possible new sowing deadlines for Finland and technical changes in EU regional base areas for cereals compensation.
The main session will consider bids to export wheat, barley and rye from the open market. Traders can bid for subsidies or offer taxes, though current prices point to refunds only.

The main meeting agenda also includes "possible" bidding for a tender to export 209,667 tonnes of rye from German intervention stores. But the tender failed to open in time for the season's first export auction because of publication delays.
A German official said the tender was now expected to open on July 31, the date of the next EU grain committee meeting.
